page_data.en:
Original Su D 2381/15

COPY

Special Branch,
July 22, 1935.

S. 5

In order to ensure that no literature in
Chinese which is undesirable from a police
point of view, will escape detection, the
officer in charge of S. 5 should use one or
two detectives to make regular visits to shops
and other places where literature is sold and
send out a clerk to check their work as often
as one can be spared, but not less than once per
week. The detectives engaged on this duty and
the clerks sent out to check their work should
submit a report each Monday morning giving a list
of the shops visited during the previous week and
the result of their observations in each establishment.

(sd.) T.P.G.
D.C. Special Branch.

P.S. This is a supplement to the general instructions.
page_data.zh:
原件 Su D 2381/15

副本

特务科，
1935年7月22日。

S. 5

为确保从警方角度来看不良的中文文献不被漏查，S. 5 的负责人应指派一至两名侦探定期走访销售文献的商店和其他场所，并尽可能经常（但每周不少于一次）派出一名文员去核查他们的工作。从事此项工作的侦探以及被派去核查其工作的文员，应在每周一上午提交一份报告，列出上周走访的商店名单以及在每家机构的观察结果。

(签名) T.P.G.
特务科副督察长。

附言：这是对一般指令的补充。

Ss. 5 

In order to ensure that no literature in 
Chinese which is undesirable from a police 
point of view, will escape detection, the 
officer in charre of S. 5 should use one or 
two detectives to make regular visits to shops 
and other places where literature is sold and 
send out a clerk to check their work as often 
as one can be — but not less than once per 
week. The detecitves engaged on this duty and 
the clerks sent out to check their work should 
submit a revort each Monday morning giving a list 
of the shops visited during the previous week and 


the result of their observations in each establishment.
